title: $p^*$ preserves the unit
statement:
Give $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $\Sh((\Spec\Z)_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$
the tensor products of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], whose units are the
constant sheaves $\Z$. The functor $p_*$ is lax monoidal. By the adjunction
[def-sfb-point-adjunction], $p^*$ is therefore oplax monoidal. Its unit
comparison morphism $p^*\Z\to\Z$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $C=*_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $D=(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z)_{\mathrm{proét}}$, $a_C,a_D$ for sheafification, $i_C,i_D$ for inclusion of sheaves, and $r$ for presheaf restriction along $u^{\mathrm{op}}$. Fix a universe in which the sites have sets of objects and arrows and the abelian value category admits colimits of those sizes, using the essentially small site convention of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $a_C,a_D$ are strong monoidal for the objectwise presheaf tensor product and the stated sheaf tensors, and the units are $a_C\underline{\mathbf Z},a_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] we have $a_D\dashv i_D$. Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates] to its strong monoidal left adjoint: $i_D$ is lax monoidal. With the sheaf tensor unit defined as $a_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$, the canonical strong unit comparison of $a_D$ is the identity. Thus its right adjoint's lax unit $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to i_Da_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$ is the sheafification unit: it is the mate of the inverse strong unit comparison of $a_D$.

source.place: First paragraph: monoidal sheafification and its right adjoint

proof.text: Restriction $r$ is strong monoidal: at $S$ both $r(P\otimes Q)$ and $rP\otimes rQ$ are $P(uS)\otimes Q(uS)$, and its unit comparison is the identity on $\mathbf Z$. Thus $a_C r i_D$ is lax monoidal by composing these structure maps: the tensor map first uses the tensor comparison for $a_Cr$, then applies $a_Cr$ to that of $i_D$; the unit map is the analogous composite. The coherence diagrams reduce to the respective diagrams for these three functors by functoriality. By [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-continuous], $ri_DG$ is already a sheaf, so the sheafification counit identifies $a_Cri_D$ with the restriction functor $p_*$ of [def-sfb-point-lower-star]. It is an isomorphism since the sheafification universal property applied to a sheaf gives an inverse to its counit. Transport the structure along this identification. Explicitly its tensor map is the unique sheaf map from $a_C(ri_DF\otimes ri_DG)$ induced by restricting the map $i_DF\otimes i_DG\to i_Da_D(i_DF\otimes i_DG)$. Its unit $e:a_C\underline{\mathbf Z}\to p_*a_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$ is uniquely determined by $i_C(e)\circ k_{\underline{\mathbf Z}}=r(k'_{\underline{\mathbf Z}})$, where $k,k'$ are the sheafification units on $C,D$. These descriptions follow by the unit universal properties in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

source.place: First paragraph: the restriction lax structure and its actual unit map

proof.text: Use the canonical adjunction [def-sfb-point-adjunction]: by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], its Hom bijections are the composite of the Kan-extension and sheafification adjunctions, restricted to source sheaves. Its hypotheses hold because the sites have the size fixed in step 1 and restriction takes sheaves to sheaves by [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-continuous]. Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-mates] to this lax structure on $p_*$. This gives the oplax structure on $p^*$, whose unit comparison $h:p^*a_C\underline{\mathbf Z}\to a_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$ is precisely the adjoint of the map $e$ in step 2.

source.place: Statement: the oplax structure is transferred under the given adjunction

proof.text:
Put $T=a_D\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}$ on presheaves. The Kan-extension adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-left-exact], clause 1, applied to $b=u$; [def-sfb-point-upper-star] identifies $p^*$ with $T i_C$. For every presheaf $Q$ and sheaf $H$ on $D$, it and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T i_Ca_CQ,H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_Ca_CQ,ri_DH)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Q,ri_DH)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(TQ,H).$$
The middle bijection is precomposition with $k_Q:Q\to i_Ca_CQ$; it applies because $ri_DH$ is a sheaf by [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-continuous]. The composite is precomposition with $T(k_Q)$, so $T(k_Q)$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, for $f:A\to B$ inducing these bijections, surjectivity for $H=A$ gives $g:B\to A$ with $gf=1_A$, and injectivity for $H=B$ then gives $fg=1_B$. This proves the required compatibility with sheafification without assuming that restriction commutes with sheafification on arbitrary presheaves.

source.place: Second paragraph: sheafified Kan extension inverts source sheafification units; Stacks 00VE, 00VF, 00WH

proof.text: To compute $\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}\underline{\mathbf Z}$, apply the formula in [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-left-exact], clause 1. At $V\in D$ the index is $I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$, where $I_V$ has objects $(S,\phi:V\to uS)$ and arrows $f:S\to S'$ with $u(f)\phi=\phi'$. Its diagram is constant $\mathbf Z$ with identity transition maps. Use the essentially small site convention of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]: choose the sites in a universe in which their objects and arrows are sets and their abelian groups admit colimits of that size, so the cited small-category formula applies. In particular the pairs and arrows above form sets. The one-point profinite set $*$ is terminal because every profinite set has exactly one map to it. By [lem-sfb-profinite-to-proetale-finite-limits], $u$ preserves this empty limit, so $u(*)$ is terminal in $D$. For every $V$, the object $t_V=(*,V\to u(*))$ is terminal in $I_V$: from $(S,\phi)$ the unique map is $S\to *$, and its required equation holds because there is only one map $V\to u(*)$. Thus $I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$ is nonempty and connected: every object is linked to $t_V$ by the opposite of this arrow. No existence of other finite limits or general filtered-colimit theorem is needed for this connectedness argument.

source.place: Third paragraph: pointwise Kan formula and connectedness (only the terminal-object part of finite-limit preservation is needed); Stacks 00VE, 00VF

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram], the constant $\mathbf Z$ diagram on the nonempty connected category $I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$ of step 5 has colimit $\mathbf Z$, with identity legs. Hence the map $c:\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\underline{\mathbf Z}$ induced by identity maps from every copy of $\mathbf Z$ is an isomorphism at every $V$. It is natural: for $g:V'\to V$ the index functor sends $(S,\phi)$ to $(S,\phi g)$, and the restriction map is the identity after these colimit identifications, as one checks on every colimit leg. Moreover $c$ is the Kan adjoint of the identity $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to r\underline{\mathbf Z}$: the Kan adjunction sends this identity to the cocone whose leg at $(S,\phi)$ is the identity. This also follows directly from the Kan universal property and the formula in [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-left-exact].

source.place: Third paragraph: connected constant colimit, naturality and the canonical comparison

proof.text: Set $Q=\underline{\mathbf Z}$ and $B=a_D\underline{\mathbf Z}$. The map $h\circ T(k_Q):TQ\to B$ corresponds under the composite Kan/sheafification adjunctions to $i_C(e)\circ k_Q=r(k'_Q)$ by steps 2 and 3. The map $a_D(c):TQ\to B$ corresponds to exactly the same presheaf map: $c$ is adjoint to the identity, and postcomposing its target with $k'_Q$ gives $r(k'_Q)$. Thus $h\circ T(k_Q)=a_D(c)$ by injectivity of the composite Hom bijection specified by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] and the adjunction bijections in [def-sfb-point-adjunction], [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-pullback-left-exact]. Step 4 makes $T(k_Q)$ invertible and step 6 makes $c$ invertible. Sheafification sends an inverse to an inverse, so $a_D(c)$ is invertible and consequently so is $h$. This proves the required unit comparison, with the tensor units identified as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor].

source.place: Final sentences: identification and invertibility of the actual oplax unit comparison
